foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Red Sea maritime disruption sustains energy repricing via oil macro shock, with 64% pressure and 76% state confirmation, keeping the base case near 68% over 30 days.
foil.perspective_strategic: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through oil macro shock, with 64% pressure and 76% state confirmation is setting the strategic baseline, and the current 65% probability implies a live but not settled risk path.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The current 75% confidence level still leaves room for reversal; if that restraint persists, the forecast can move below the 65% baseline to 57%. Headlines like 'Oil prices set for sharp weekly fall after midterm elections' suggest market actors may prioritize containment.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Red Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 65%.
foil.top_signal: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through oil macro shock, with 64% pressure and 76% state confirmation

seismic-infrastructure.absence_reason: No product publishes a seismic forecast — earthquakes are not predictable, so there is no forecast/intel alternative to azimuth's observed USGS record. This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
